purpose: Original project questions for design review, written in our own words from general design knowledge. Scope labels are project annotations. Nothing here is a quotation or a validated rule.

adoption_values.conditional: Conditional aid; verify in the current task.
adoption_values.hypothesis: Expressive or behavioral candidate; compare, do not prescribe.
adoption_values.context_only: Physical or domain finding; screen use needs separate evidence.
adoption_values.research_only: Recognize in review; not a generation default.

items.name: Vital few
items.ask: Which few parts carry most of the value here, and do they get most of the attention?
items.limit: Usage data can shift the answer; rarely used safety paths still matter.

items.name: Fit to purpose
items.ask: What job does this form do for this audience, and would a plainer form do it as well?
items.limit: Purpose can include delight or identity; do not reduce it to utility.

items.name: Worth the cost
items.ask: Does what the person gains justify the attention or effort this asks of them?
items.limit: Estimate from the actual task, not from a general rule.

items.name: Named audience
items.ask: Who specifically is this for, and what would they do differently from the next audience?
items.limit: A sketched audience is an assumption until checked.

items.name: Worn paths
items.ask: What route do people actually take, and is the design fighting it?
items.limit: Observed habit may still be unsafe; check before paving it.

items.name: Visible order
items.ask: Can someone tell what comes first, next and last without reading everything?
items.limit: Rank from content priority, not from a default template.

items.name: First foothold
items.ask: Where does attention land first, and does that spot explain where to go?
items.limit: A loud entry with no follow-through still fails.

items.name: Reveal on need
items.ask: What can wait until asked for, and is it easy to find when it is?
items.limit: Do not hide what the decision depends on.

items.name: Lead with the point
items.ask: Would the reader get the main claim if they stopped after the opening?
items.limit: Suspense can be the point in narrative work.

items.name: Sort by question
items.ask: Is this ordered by how the reader looks things up: time, place, category, rank or letter?
items.limit: One arrangement rarely serves every lookup.

items.name: Narrative arc
items.ask: Does each step give a reason to read the next?
items.limit: Do not force a story onto reference material.

items.name: Know where you are
items.ask: Can someone tell where they are, where they can go, and how to get back?
items.limit: Very short pieces may not need any of this.

items.name: Swappable parts
items.ask: Which pieces can change independently without breaking neighbors?
items.limit: Modules that differ in purpose should stay separate.

items.name: Line up
items.ask: Do edges and centers relate on purpose, judged by eye rather than bounding box?
items.limit: Optical correction is not equal widths; judge the render.

items.name: Near means related
items.ask: Does spacing alone show what belongs together?
items.limit: Containers are not wrong, but test spacing first.

items.name: Alike means related
items.ask: Do things that look alike behave alike, and the reverse?
items.limit: Consistency is not sameness; meaningful difference should show.

items.name: Shared frame
items.ask: Does a line, region or color link what the content links?
items.limit: Too many frames compete with the content.

items.name: Reads as a whole
items.ask: Will the eye complete and follow the shape you intend?
items.limit: Check at real size; thin implied shapes can vanish.

items.name: Figure and ground
items.ask: Is it clear what is in front and what is behind?
items.limit: Deliberate ambiguity is allowed if it is the idea.

items.name: Color with a job
items.ask: What does each color signal, and does the signal survive without hue?
items.limit: Cultural meaning varies; measure contrast on the real surface.

items.name: Emphasis budget
items.ask: Is only a small share emphasized, so emphasis still works?
items.limit: Set the amount from the content, not a fixed ratio.

items.name: Odd one out
items.ask: What single difference should be remembered, and is it the only one?
items.limit: Compare against a plainer candidate.

items.name: Stable appearance
items.ask: Does one thing stay recognizable across sizes and states?
items.limit: Allow scale-specific redrawing when a form breaks.

items.name: Conflict slows reading
items.ask: Does any label, color or position contradict what it stands for?
items.limit: Test with real labels, not lorem text.

items.name: Balance by weight
items.ask: Is the balance something you can defend from this composition, not from a formula?
items.limit: Grid and ratio formulas are starting points, never proof.

items.name: Full or empty
items.ask: Does this density suit the audience, rather than a habit of airiness or cramming?
items.limit: Density carries meaning in both directions.

items.name: Legible letters
items.ask: Can each letter be told apart at the real size, surface and distance?
items.limit: Print-era numbers are not screen thresholds; test the render.

items.name: Readable sentences
items.ask: Do the wording, line length and spacing suit this reader?
items.limit: Formula scores do not prove comprehension.

items.name: Cut what adds nothing
items.ask: What can go with nothing lost, and what does each remaining part add?
items.limit: Simple is not always empty; do not cut needed cues.

items.name: Simplest sufficient
items.ask: Between options that work equally, which needs the fewest parts?
items.limit: Only applies once both truly work.

items.name: Idea per unit
items.ask: How many ideas does this element carry, and can the viewer reach them?
items.limit: Dense layered meaning can be rewarding; compare candidates.

items.name: Motion shows relation
items.ask: Does moving together mean belonging together, and can the change be traced?
items.limit: Respect reduced-motion settings; motion is never the only cue.

items.name: Signals how to use
items.ask: Does it look like what it does before anyone touches it?
items.limit: Flat conventions may be learned; test with the audience.

items.name: Controls match effect
items.ask: Do position and direction of a control predict its result?
items.limit: Platform convention can outweigh geometry.

items.name: Shows what is possible
items.ask: Can people see the current state and the available actions?
items.limit: Do not expose everything at equal weight.

items.name: Recognize, not recall
items.ask: Are choices on screen rather than held in memory?
items.limit: Experts may prefer commands; offer both when it matters.

items.name: Fits their model
items.ask: Does it behave the way people already believe it works?
items.limit: Familiarity is a default, not a ceiling on invention.

items.name: Reachable targets
items.keywords: fitts target size distance pointer touch
items.ask: Are frequent or urgent targets large and close, and risky ones further away?
items.limit: Measure on the real input device.

items.name: Fewer choices, faster
items.ask: Does the number of options slow a repeated, simple decision?
items.limit: Do not turn this into a menu-count limit; grouping can help more.

items.name: Limit wrong moves
items.ask: Can invalid actions be made impossible rather than reported afterwards?
items.limit: Do not block legitimate edge cases.

items.name: Easy to undo
items.ask: What happens after a mistake, and how much effort does recovery take?
items.limit: Reserve confirmation for what cannot be undone.

items.name: User in charge
items.ask: Can people pause, leave or adjust without losing work?
items.limit: More options can also mean more load.

items.name: Mental and physical load
items.ask: How much must someone remember, compute or do to finish?
items.limit: Count on the actual path, not on the sketch.

items.name: Expect bad input
items.ask: What happens with long, empty, malformed or missing content?
items.limit: Test real extremes, and do not invent customer data.

items.name: Margin for the unknown
items.ask: How far past normal use does this keep working?
items.limit: Spend margin where failure is costly.

items.name: Weakest point
items.ask: Which single failure takes the rest down, and is there a fallback?
items.limit: Some failures should fail loudly on purpose.

items.name: Does not simply scale
items.ask: What breaks when size, count or language changes?
items.limit: Check each size that actually ships.

items.name: Small chunks
items.ask: Is the material split into units someone can hold and check?
items.limit: Do not turn memory research into a hard count limit.

items.name: Build on what they know
items.ask: What known idea can introduce the unknown one?
items.limit: Check the bridge exists for this audience.

items.name: Learn by steps
items.ask: Does complexity arrive only after the previous step works?
items.limit: Experts need a way to skip.

items.name: Engage to remember
items.ask: Does the viewer have to do something with the idea?
items.limit: Recall claims need a test; do not assert uplift.

items.name: Borrow with care
items.ask: What does the borrowed form promise, and does this deliver it?
items.limit: Copying a surface without the reason fails the layer test.

items.name: Physical analogy limit
items.ask: Is a physical-space finding being applied to a screen without evidence?
items.limit: Needs separate screen evidence before use.

items.name: Beauty buys patience
items.ask: Is appeal hiding a problem in testing?
items.limit: Perceived ease is not measured ease.

items.name: Compare fairly
items.ask: Are the things compared on the same basis and the same scale?
items.limit: Framing decides meaning; show the base.

items.name: Seen is not noticed
items.ask: What could a reviewer overlook because they were looking for something else?
items.limit: Use a fresh look or a list from the render.

items.name: What they say vs do
items.ask: Are stated preference and measured performance kept apart?
items.limit: Both can matter; report them separately.

items.name: Hoped-for results
items.ask: Could the reviewer's expectations be producing the result?
items.limit: Declare when the author is also the tester.

items.name: Observation changes it
items.ask: Is the measurement changing what it measures?
items.limit: State the limit rather than dropping the test.

items.name: Too many owners
items.ask: Is the result an average of opinions, with no one able to defend it?
items.limit: Consensus may be right for safety or standards.

items.name: Own-idea bias
items.ask: Is an existing solution being rejected only because it is not ours?
items.limit: Reuse still needs rights and fit checks.

items.name: Build to learn
items.ask: What is the cheapest version that answers this question?
items.limit: A prototype passing is not the product passing.

items.name: Good enough stop
items.ask: Is stopping here honest about what remains unverified?
items.limit: State the residual risk.

items.name: Feelings as a hypothesis
items.keywords: emotion warmth nature face character archetype
items.ask: What feeling is intended, and how will you check it arrived?
items.limit: Compare candidates; do not prescribe a look.

items.name: Familiar yet new
items.ask: Is this new enough to notice, yet recognizable enough to accept?
items.limit: Originality can justify unfamiliar form when it works.

items.name: Sticks in memory
items.ask: What concrete thing would someone repeat later?
items.limit: Working surfaces may rightly be forgettable.

items.name: Imperfect on purpose
items.ask: Does irregularity carry meaning, or is it a faked surface?
items.limit: Faked material fails the layer test.

items.name: Immersion and focus
items.ask: What must vanish so attention stays on the work?
items.limit: Immersion cannot hide a broken task.

items.name: Persuasion ethics
items.keywords: nudge scarcity priming framing dark pattern
items.ask: Would this cue still be acceptable if the person could see how it works?
items.limit: Recognize it in review; not a generation default.

items.name: Appearance bias
items.ask: Is imagery relying on a stereotype or a contested claim about people?
items.limit: Do not turn these claims into casting or styling rules.
